result.title: Ghana's First Marine Sanctuary & Indigenous Forest Protection | WEF | Top Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:16 - Ghana's first marine sanctuary: Almost 200 countries across the world have pledged to protect 30% of their ocean by 2030. But right now, there’s a lot of work to do, with just 10% of the global ocean protected. #Ghana just took a big step forward with the establishment of the Greater Cape Three Points marine protected area.

01.56 - AI satellites re-shaping Earth observation: Orbitworks plans to launch a 10-satellite constellation later this year. Rather than capturing images in orbit and transmitting them back to Earth for analysis, which creates a time lag, the satellites will use #AI to process data directly in space. CEO Hamdullah Mohib is a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader. Here, he explains how the technology works.

04.24 - Japan's new word for extreme heat: In 2007, Japanese weather forecasters began to use a new word - ‘moshobi’, meaning extremely hot day - to describe when the mercury climbed past 35˚C. 

05.53 - Empowering indigenous forest protection: Indigenous cultures have a lot to teach the world, says Indonesian rainforest activist Bustar Maitar. And the first thing is to respect nature by taking from it only what you need. Maitar enjoyed a successful career with Greenpeace, winning ‘zero deforestation’ pledges from major multinationals. But he was drawn back to Papua to fight for forests there - and also, through his EcoNusa Foundation, to defend the rights, culture and livelihoods of #Indigenous communities, from which will emerge the next generation of #forest stewards.

result.title: Japan has coined a new term for extremely hot weather
result.description:
Do you know your ‘moshobi’ from your ‘kokushobi’?

In 2007, Japanese weather forecasters began to use a new word - ‘moshobi’, meaning extremely hot day - to describe when the mercury climbed past 35˚C. 

This year, rising global temperatures have prompted #Japan to add to its weather lexicon once again. ‘Kokushobi’ means ‘cruelly hot day’, and forecasters are using it for temperatures of 40˚C and higher. 

Last summer was Japan's hottest on record, and the country’s weather experts are predicting another scorching season this year, too.

result.title: What is 'Summer Davos’?
result.description:
Technology is increasingly shaping the world economy. 

That's why more than 1,700 leaders from science, technology, business and government will gather in Dalian, a major innovation hub in north-east China, for the Annual Meeting of the New Champions.

Taking place at the centre of one of the world's most dynamic technology and manufacturing ecosystems, this year's 'Summer Davos' will explore the ideas and industries shaping the decade ahead.

The theme for this year’s meeting is ‘Innovating at Scale’, and participants will be focused on discussing how new technologies can create resilient, inclusive growth.

Sessions will be livestreamed on our website and you can follow along at #AMNC26.

result.title: How to navigate a crisis: lessons from a chief investment officer
result.description:
On this episode we team up with The View Beyond, a podcast from wealth management group Julius Baer, to discuss how to navigate crises.
Julius Baer's Group Chief Investment Officer Yves Bonzon gives his perspective as someone who has spent decades making high-stakes decisions on behalf of investors.

This episode is a collaboration with The View Beyond, the weekend edition of Moving Markets, Julius Baer’s daily flagship podcast on the markets, thematic investing, and wealth management. The co-host is Moving Markets host Bernadette Anderko. result.title: 5 leaders from NVIDIA, Goldman Sachs and more share career advice for uncertain times
result.description:
Top leaders from NVIDIA, Walmart International, TIAA, Goldman Sachs and NYU share career advice, leadership lessons and practical ways to stay resilient through uncertainty in an AI age. This an inspiring collection of advice and personal anecdotes shared at this spring's commencement addresses can help anyone from new grads to veteran professionals navigate coming AI shifts and other big career pivots.
In this episode:
• NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang on AI and maximizing your potential
• TIAA CEO Thasunda Brown Duckett on the advice she gives her team
• Social Psychologist Jonathan Haidt's 3 tips on how to have an amazing life
• Former Walmart CEO Kathryn McLay's advice on the early career moment that helped her keep perspective
• Goldman Sachs Chairman & CEO David Solomon on why he still DJs - and the importance of cultivating passions outside of work
